items.note: Subgradients are taken in Euclidean space: subgradientFamily F p is g ↦ g on ∂F(p), with range euclideanVector '' ∂F(p). V(p) = jumpSpace (vectorSpan of the range) = span(S -ᵥ S), S the Euclidean copy of ∂F(p); U(p) = tangentSpace = V(p)ᗮ; a(p) = canonicalVector hF p = EuclideanGeometry.orthogonalProjection (aff ∂F(p)) 0 (decomposition_notation). ∂F(p) is the global supporting set ConvexSubdifferential.subdifferential (nonempty for finite convex F).
With line 16 ("Hence every subgradient satisfies"): for every g ∈ ∂F(p), the orthogonal projection of g onto U(p) is a(p), and ⟪g, a(p)⟫ = ‖a(p)‖² (Euclidean pairing of euclideanVector g).
(A:AC) at p is AffineCorrectAt F p := IsAffineCritical F p → 0 ∈ ∂F(p); IsAffineCritical F p is 0 ∈ aff ∂F(p) for the Euclidean copy, equivalently (ac_def) 0 ∈ affineSpan ℝ (∂F(p)) in ℝⁿ.
With line 36 ("Consider"): the library objective AffineRankLoss.objective x = x₀ + x₀² + x₁² + |x₀x₁| (u = x₀, v = x₁) equals max of its branches u+u²+v²+uv and u+u²+v²-uv.

The proof of the local correctness statement (prose/026). Its displays are disp/006 and disp/007; formula_positive_near states the undisplayed step "It remains positive nearby"; the subdifferential of a finite smooth maximum is the convex hull of the active gradients (subdifferential_eq_active_convexHull).

Standing assumptions: those of prose/026; A is a variable with A p = augmentedLast (active gradients at p), the matrix with columns (∇f_i(p), 1), i ∈ I_* (last row of ones), and lastTarget n = (0,…,0,1). Claims: A(p)λ = (0,…,0,1)ᵀ iff ∑λ_i = 1 and ∑λ_i∇f_i(p) = 0; and at every affine-critical p near x_* there is such λ vanishing on the indices of I_* inactive at p (the zero extension).
With "Full column rank at x_* persists nearby": near x_*, A(p) is injective, det(A(p)ᵀA(p)) ≠ 0, and every solution of A(p)λ = (0,…,0,1)ᵀ equals (A(p)ᵀA(p))⁻¹A(p)ᵀ(0,…,0,1)ᵀ.

In the setting of prose/026 (restricted family I_*), for every p near x_*: if p_j → p and the active set at every p_j is a fixed nonempty J ⊆ I(p), then γ(p_j) → dist(0, aff{∇f_i(p) : i ∈ J}) (subfamilyDistance) and this limit is ≥ γ(p).

items.title: A low-level affine-critical gap
items.note: F finite convex (ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ F), semialgebraic (IsSemialgebraicObjective: the graph {(x, F(x))} is defined by a quantifier-free Boolean polynomial formula, semialgebraic_objective_def), attaining F_* (IsLeast (Set.range F) Fstar). Conclusion: ∃ ε > 0, ∀ p, F p < F_* + ε → 0 ∈ affineSpan ℝ (∂F(p)) → 0 ∈ ∂F(p).

The proof of Proposition A:semialgebraic. Displays: disp/010-012. Undisplayed steps proved in the library: the subgradient (support) graph is semialgebraic (supportGraph_semialgebraic), an affine representation of zero with at most n+1 subgradients (isAffineCritical_iff_bounded_supports), the finite cover by pieces connected by piecewise C^∞ paths (semialgebraic_finite_path_cover), regularity of F∘p (convex_semialgebraic_objective_curve_piecewise_smooth), (F∘p)' = 0 at affine-critical points (derivative_zero_of_affineCritical), constancy along paths and finitely many values (finitely_many_values).

Under the hypotheses of the proposition: Ĉ_aff = affineCriticalGraph F = {v | v none = F(v ∘ some) ∧ IsAffineCritical F (v ∘ some)} (coordinates Option (Fin n), none = value), and both C_aff and Ĉ_aff are semialgebraic.

Standing assumptions: the proposition's, a path p inside C_aff on [0,1] (a piece of the cover), an interior t where p and F∘p are differentiable, g ∈ ∂F(p(t)). Claim: u ↦ F(p(u)) - gᵀp(u) has a local minimum at t (in fact a global one, by the supporting inequality).
Under the standing assumptions of disp/011 with p'(t) = v (HasDerivAt) and (F∘p)'(t) = a: a = gᵀv for every g ∈ ∂F(p(t)).

items.anchor: Affine balance concerns equal-rate descent, whereas convex balance concerns stationarity.
items.note: For finite convex F: 0 ∉ aff ∂F(p) iff some v has gᵀv = -1 for all g ∈ ∂F(p) (equal-rate descent); 0 ∈ ∂F(p) iff p minimizes F (stationarity).

items.anchor: This distinction gives useful local geometry but does not by itself force an algorithm to visit it.
items.reason: Scope remark: the geometric results of the chapter say nothing about the iterates of an algorithm (the dynamical theorems are in Chapters C and U).

items.reason: History of the source: the chapter keeps the geometric propositions of the original affine-criticality note.
items.note: Wording point W5 applied on 15 October 2026. Before: "This module preserves the geometric propositions of the affine-criticality note~Chapter~\ref{comp:A}." ("note Chapter 8" inside Chapter 8, from the citation map of \cite{SA}).

items.anchor: They do not depend on the BFGS principal-minor lemma.
items.reason: Statement about proof dependencies: the geometric results of the chapter (and their Lean proofs, e.g. local_affine_critical_correctness, semialgebraic_low_affine_critical_gap) use no principal-minor result.

items.anchor: The originally proposed dynamical step is now proved only in the completed settings of Chapters
items.note: The dynamical step, a theorem forcing an affine-critical cluster point (line 115), is proved in Chapter C (Theorem C:thm:cluster, word for word the article's Theorem art:planar-cluster) and in Chapter U (Theorem 11.2, section "A forced affine-critical cluster-point theorem"): the targets of prose/041. "only" and the clause "no blanket theorem for all finite smooth maxima is asserted" describe the scope and assert nothing (the general case is the OPEN conjecture prose/042).

items.anchor: The affine hull equals $a(p)+V(p)$ and $a(p)\perp V(p)$.
items.note: z ∈ aff ∂F(p) iff z - a(p) ∈ V(p), and a(p) ∈ V(p)ᗮ (Euclidean).

items.anchor: is therefore equivalent, at every nonoptimal point under consideration, to the existence of a direction $v$
items.note: At every p ∉ argmin F: AffineCorrectAt F p ↔ ∃ v, ∀ g ∈ ∂F(p), gᵀv = -1.

items.anchor: One may take $v=-a(p)/\|a(p)\|^2$.
items.note: At a nonoptimal point where (A:AC) holds, p is not affine critical; then a(p) ≠ 0 and ⟪g, -a(p)/‖a(p)‖²⟫ = -1 for every g ∈ ∂F(p).

items.anchor: Conversely such an equal-rate direction rules out zero in the affine hull.
items.note: (∃ v, ∀ g ∈ ∂F(p), gᵀv = -1) → ¬ IsAffineCritical F p.

items.anchor: This is stronger than ordinary strict descent, which requires only negative, not equal, inner products.
items.note: Every equal-rate direction has gᵀv < 0 for all g ∈ ∂F(p); conversely F(x) = max(x, 2x) at p = 0 has the strict descent direction v = -1 but no equal-rate direction (1, 2 ∈ ∂F(0)).

items.anchor: On a compact admissible run, all cluster points share the limiting value $\ell$.
items.note: "Compact admissible run": all iterates in a compact K. Then F(x_k) → ℓ for some ℓ, and F(p) = ℓ for every cluster point p.

items.anchor: If at least one cluster point is affine critical and \eqref{A:AC} holds on the basin, that point is optimal
items.note: With the next sentence ("Compactness gives convergence to the solution set, and uniqueness gives convergence of the entire sequence"): run in compact K ("the basin"), (A:AC) on K, an affine-critical cluster point p: p minimizes F, F(x_k) → F(p) = F_* (so ℓ = F_*), Euclidean dist(x_k, argmin F) → 0, and x_k → p if p is the unique minimizer.

items.anchor: This reduction does not assume an iterate limit.
items.note: cluster_reduction assumes only a cluster point (MapClusterPt), not convergence of (x_k).

items.anchor: It would be incorrect to replace affine criticality of a cluster point by vanishing gradients at differentiable iterates
items.note: For F(x) = |x| on ℝ: every gradient at x ≠ 0 has norm 1; the admissible run x_k = (-1/2)^k (absRun) converges to the minimizer 0, its cluster point 0 is affine critical, yet ‖g_k‖ = 1 for all k: vanishing gradients is not available as a substitute hypothesis.

items.anchor: Let $\gamma(p)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\operatorname{aff}\partial F(p))$.
items.note: γ(p) = AffineDistance.objectiveDistance F p = Metric.infDist 0 (aff of the Euclidean copy of ∂F(p)); for convex F it equals ‖a(p)‖ and is positive iff p is not affine critical (gamma_def).

items.anchor: A useful quantitative condition is a positive minimum of $\gamma$ on every compact positive objective band.
items.note: PositiveGapOnBands F F_*: on every band {F_* + η ≤ F ≤ b} (η > 0) that is compact and nonempty, γ attains a strictly positive minimum. "useful" is not a claim; prose/032 shows what the condition gives (visibility).

items.anchor: Pointwise nonvanishing plus compactness does not establish it when ranks change.
items.note: For the rank-loss example (F_* = -1/4): γ > 0 at every point with F > F_*, every band {F_* + η ≤ F ≤ b} is compact, yet PositiveGapOnBands fails (on {-1/8 ≤ F ≤ 1}, γ(0,t) = 2|t| → 0).

items.anchor: Both branch Hessians have eigenvalues $1$ and $3$, so $F$ is strongly convex, with unique minimizer $(-1/2,0)$ and value $-1/4$.
items.note: Each branch is C^∞ with Hessian matrix (RadialHessian.matrix, the matrix of the second derivative) [[2, ±1], [±1, 2]], symmetric, eigenvalues exactly 1 and 3; each branch and F are strongly convex with modulus 1 (F - ½‖x‖² convex, Euclidean); F(-1/2, 0) = -1/4 is the minimum value, attained only there.

items.anchor: At $(0,t)$, $t\ne0$, the active gradients are $(1+t,2t)$ and $(1-t,2t)$, giving $\gamma(0,t)=2|t|$.
items.note: Both branches are active at (0,t), with gradients (1+t, 2t) and (1-t, 2t); ∂F(0,t) is their convex hull; γ(0,t) = 2|t| for t ≠ 0.

items.anchor: At zero the gradient is $(1,0)$, so $\gamma(0,0)=1$.
items.note: F is differentiable at 0 with gradient (1,0) (F(x) - F(0) - x₀ = x₀² + x₁² + |x₀x₁| = O(‖x‖²)), and γ(0) = 1.

items.anchor: On the other switching axis $\gamma(u,0)=|1+2u|$, vanishing only at the optimizer.
items.note: γ(u,0) = |1 + 2u|, and γ(u,0) = 0 iff (u,0) = (-1/2, 0), the optimizer.

items.anchor: Smooth points are affine critical only when stationary.
items.note: At every point where the example F is differentiable with gradient g: affine critical iff g = 0 (a consequence of the general affineCritical_iff_gradient_zero for finite convex F).

items.anchor: Thus \eqref{A:AC} holds globally, but $\gamma(0,t)\to0$ while the objective gap tends to $1/4$.
items.note: AffineCorrectAt F x for every x; γ(0,t) → 0 and F(0,t) - F(-1/2,0) → 1/4 as t → 0, t ≠ 0.

items.anchor: This is a geometric rank-loss example, not a BFGS counterexample.
items.reason: Classification of the example (no BFGS run is constructed or claimed to fail); nothing to prove.

items.anchor: A sufficiently small neighborhood of its actual optimizer excludes the rank-loss point.
items.note: The rank loss happens at the origin along the axis {u = 0} (γ(0,t) → 0 ≠ γ(0,0) = 1); the neighborhood {u < -1/4} of the optimizer (-1/2, 0) contains no point of that axis, in particular not the origin.

items.anchor: Let $F=\max_{i\le m}f_i$ with convex $C^1$ branches and a minimizer $x_*$.
items.note: The unnumbered statement of lines 51-56 with display disp/005. F = max_i f_i (IsGreatest of the finite family at every x), convex C¹ branches (ContDiff ℝ 1), x_* a minimizer, I_* = activeIndices F f x_* enumerated by activeIndexMap, the active gradients (coordinateGradient) affinely independent, weights λ*_i > 0 on I_* with ∑λ* = 1 and ∑λ*_i∇f_i(x_*) = 0. Conclusions: inactive branches have f_i(x_*) < F(x_*) and near x_* every active index is in I_* ("disappear in a sufficiently small neighborhood"); (A:AC) holds at every point of a neighborhood of x_*.

items.anchor: This is the source note's barycentric-stability argument
items.reason: Provenance and classification (relation to the source note and the cited nondegeneracy results; not a BFGS convergence theorem).

items.anchor: There is also local lower semicontinuity of $\gamma$.
items.note: In the setting of prose/026, γ is lower semicontinuous at every point of a neighborhood of x_*.

items.anchor: For each nonempty $J\subset I_*$, the distance to the affine hull of the gradients in $J$ is continuous
items.note: Near x_*, for every nonempty J ⊆ I_*, q ↦ dist(0, aff{∇f_i(q) : i ∈ J}) (subfamilyDistance) is continuous at p. The reason given (nonsingular Gram matrix) is the library proof (closest point by the Gram-inverse formula, affine_distance_eq_formula), with affine independence persisting near x_* (eventually_affineIndependent).

items.anchor: For $p_j\to p$, pass to a subsequence of constant active set $J\subset I(p)$.
items.note: Near x_*, for every p_j → p there are a strictly increasing φ and a nonempty J ⊆ I(p) (active indices of I_* at p) with active set J at every p_{φ(j)} (eventual inclusion of active sets plus pigeonhole).

items.anchor: On a compact positive band, local \eqref{A:AC} therefore gives a strictly positive minimum.
items.note: There is a neighborhood V of x_* such that on every nonempty compact K ⊆ V with F > F(x_*) on K, γ attains a strictly positive minimum.

items.anchor: This establishes visibility, not the full transport needed in arbitrary dimension.
items.note: A bound γ ≥ γ₀ > 0 on a set S gives the visibility condition (V) of Chapter T on S for the PSD field W(x) = a(x)a(x)ᵀ: gᵀW(x)g = ‖a(x)‖⁴ ≥ γ₀⁴ at every differentiable x ∈ S. The clause "not the full transport needed in arbitrary dimension" is a caveat (no transport claim).

items.anchor: Here and below, a piecewise $C^1$ path is continuous on $[0,1]$ and $C^1$ at every interior parameter outside a finite set.
items.note: With the next sentence ("No derivative at 0 or 1, or derivative extension across a junction, is required."): PiecewiseC1 p := ContinuousOn p [0,1] ∧ ∃ finite S, ∀ t ∈ (0,1) \ S, ContDiffAt ℝ 1 p t. The library's paths (PiecewiseSmoothPath, C^∞ off a finite set) are piecewise C¹ (piecewiseC1_of_smooth).

items.anchor: The geometric facts used above are established by real-polynomial projection
items.reason: Description of how the facts used in the proof are established (proof methods) and of the role of the references; all those facts are proved in Lean (proof/002's list).
items.note: Wording point W5 applied on 15 October 2026: "the references~\cite{BDLS} supply" (before "the references~\cite{BDLS}; Chapter~\ref{comp:A} supply", a self-citation from the citation map of \cite{SA,BDLS}).

items.anchor: The affine-critical set also has finitely many actual semialgebraic path classes
items.note: With the next sentence ("Each class is semialgebraic and internally connected by such paths"). The relation (a path continuous on [0,1] inside C_aff whose graph over [0,1] is semialgebraic) is an equivalence relation on C_aff; its classes are finitely many, semialgebraic, and connected by such paths.

items.anchor: Every continuous semialgebraic path admits the finite-exception regularity just specified on the same curve
items.note: A path continuous on [0,1] with semialgebraic graph is itself piecewise C¹ (C^∞ off a finite set of interior parameters); for finite convex semialgebraic F, F∘p is continuous on [0,1] and C^∞ off finitely many interior parameters.

items.anchor: The objective is constant on each class.
items.note: F p = F q for p, q in the same path class of C_aff.

items.anchor: Ordinary topological connected components are separately finite and semialgebraic, with constant objective value
items.note: The connected components (connectedComponentIn) of C_aff are finitely many and semialgebraic, and F is constant on each. The clause "their identification with path classes is not needed here" makes no claim.

items.anchor: This proposition concerns affine criticality rather than merely Clarke criticality.
items.note: Every Clarke-critical point (0 ∈ ∂F(p), for convex F exactly the minimizers) is affine critical, so the proposition controls the larger set of affine-critical points.

items.anchor: It does not imply local BFGS convergence without a dynamical theorem forcing an affine-critical cluster point.
items.reason: Scope remark: the proposition is static; with an affine-critical cluster point, prose/012 (cluster_reduction) gives convergence. No claim to prove.

items.anchor: provide such theorems under their respective additional hypotheses.
items.note: Chapter C's affine-critical cluster-point theorem in the plane (Theorem C:thm:cluster, word for word the article's Theorem art:planar-cluster) and Chapter U's Theorem 11.2 (section "A forced affine-critical cluster-point theorem").

items.anchor: The recorded general-dimensional conjecture concerns finite convex $C^{2,1}$ maxima
items.note: With display disp/013 (U_* = activeTangentSpace F f x_* i₁) and the sentence "The proposed conclusion is local full-BFGS convergence for arbitrary SPD initialization." Reading: F = max of convex C² branches with Lipschitz Hessians, unique minimizer, a compact sublevel above F_*, affinely independent active gradients, weights > 0 on I_* summing to 1 with ∑λ_i∇f_i(x_*) = 0, vᵀ(∑λ_i∇²f_i(x_*))v > 0 for 0 ≠ v ∈ U_*; conclusion: for every 0 < c₁ < c₂ < 1 some ε > 0 such that every admissible run with these constants and F(x_0) < F_* + ε (any H_0 ≻ 0) has F(x_k) → F_* and x_k → x_*. The basin may depend on the line-search constants (the planar Corollary art:planar-max even gives one independent of them). The hypotheses can all hold together (the example at the end of Ch08A: n = m = 1, one branch x²/2, x_* = 0, i₁ = 0, λ = 1; U_* = R, weighted Hessian 1).

items.anchor: The planar theorem proves a strict-contour version; the fixed-normal theorem proves a different arbitrary-dimensional class.
items.note: The planar version with strict contours instead of the weighted-Hessian condition: Chapter C's Corollary C:cor:max (the article's Corollary art:planar-max); the fixed-normal theorems of Chapter U: Theorems 11.1 and 11.2.

items.anchor: Neither establishes this full conjecture.
items.reason: Status of an open problem (prose/042 remains open); no claim to prove.

items.anchor: Straightening an active manifold by a nonlinear coordinate change does not preserve ordinary BFGS
items.note: Example: F(u,v) = max{18u² + v² + v, 2u² + v² - v} = 10u² + v² + |v + 8u²| (finite, convex), whose active manifold (both branches active) is the parabola v = -8u²; the polynomial diffeomorphism ψ(u,v) = (u, v + 8u²) straightens it into the axis {z₂ = 0} (the branches are equal iff ψ(x)₂ = 0). The accepted full BFGS step from (1,2) to (-1/5,11/6) (H_0 = I, α = 1/30; F differentiable at both points, gradients (36,5) and (-36/5,14/3); Armijo c₁ = 1/4, weak Wolfe c₂ = 1/2) is mapped by ψ to an ascent direction of F∘ψ⁻¹ (gradient (-44,5) at ψ(x_0) = (1,10), pairing 407/30 > 0), which is -αH∇(F∘ψ⁻¹) for no H ≻ 0, α > 0. The clause "and cannot supply the missing implication" is a remark on proof strategy.

The example in this chapter supplies the stated finite, strongly convex realization
items.note: The rank-loss example is a finite (two-branch) maximum, strongly convex, with γ discontinuous; the clause "the general rank-loss mechanism is not claimed as new" is a priority disclaimer.

items.anchor: The argument uses standard stability of full-rank augmented gradient systems and positive multipliers.
items.note: Describes the proof of prose/026: full column rank of the augmented system persists (disp/007) and positive multipliers stay positive (formula_positive_near), both proved in Lean.

This geometric deduction is included with its proof.
This is a corollary of established stratified projection and definable critical-value machinery
items.reason: Literature attribution (Bolte–Daniilidis–Lewis–Shiota) for Proposition A:semialgebraic, whose own proof is covered (proposition and proof/002).

items.anchor: All subgradients have the same tangential projection on a compatible smooth stratum.
items.note: The projection formula of the cited literature; along curves it is disp/012: for every path p with (F∘p)'(t) defined, every g ∈ ∂F(p(t)) has the same pairing gᵀp'(t) = (F∘p)'(t) with the velocity, i.e. the same projection onto the span of such velocities. Strata are not defined in the companion; its own proof uses the curve version.

items.anchor: Projecting an affine combination equal to zero, whose coefficients sum to one, makes that stratum gradient zero.
items.note: If a linear map P sends every g_i to the same r and ∑λ_ig_i = 0 with ∑λ_i = 1, then r = 0.
